items.title: Intersection product of two integral subschemes of a smooth integral scheme equals the fundamental class of their intersection under a dimension and Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a field k, an integral scheme X smooth over k, and integral closed subschemes Y, Z of dimensions summing to dim(X) + d, the lemma asserts that if dim(Y cap Z) <= d and O_{Y,xi} and O_{Z,xi} are Cohen-Macaulay at every point xi of the intersection of dimension d, then the intersection product [Y] . [Z] equals [Y cap Z]_d in CH_d(X) (statement lines 14522-14534). The proof identifies the intersection product with a higher codimension Gysin pullback: [Y] . [Z] = Delta^!([Y x Z]) where Delta^! is the Gysin map of the diagonal with respect to the tangent sheaf of X over k, which is locally free of rank dim(X) (proof lines 14537-14542). It then rewrites Y cap Z as the fibre product of Y x Z with X along the diagonal and notes dim(Y x Z) = dim(Y) + dim(Z), so that the first three hypotheses of the Gysin lemma are satisfied (proof lines 14542-14547). The fourth hypothesis is obtained by observing that the local map O_{Y,xi} -> O_{Y x Z,xi} is flat with fibre O_{Z,xi}, so Cohen-Macaulayness of both factors forces Cohen-Macaulayness of O_{Y x Z,xi}, after which the Gysin lemma applies (proof lines 14548-14559). Recognising the intersection product as a diagonal Gysin pullback and transporting Cohen-Macaulayness along the flat projection are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.
